display.title: The Chitas Miracle
display.summary_short: For the Rebbe Maharash's yahrzeit, two stories of the power of Chitas: the Rebbe Maharash defeats a decree in Petersburg, and a Jerusalem rosh yeshiva's legs are saved.
display.summary_long: In honor of the Rebbe Maharash's yahrzeit, the storyteller tells two miracles of learning Chitas. In 1857 the Tzemach Tzedek sent his son, the Rebbe Maharash, to Petersburg to stop the Maskilim from forcing their books on the yeshivos. He shared what he had learned years earlier at the resting place of his mother, the Alter Rebbe's daughter: the Baal Shem Tov had told her that one who knows Chumash, Tehillim and Tanya by heart can break any decree, hinted in the word 'chitas' in the Torah. The Rebbe Maharash said Chitas in every office, and the decree collapsed. The second story was told at a wedding in Jerusalem around 1954 by a rosh yeshiva whose legs were so ill that doctors planned to amputate. As a yeshiva student in Europe, he and his friends delayed helping a Jew whose horse was choking, and mocked Itche, a man everyone took for a drunkard, who warned them. Itche turned out to be a hidden tzaddik who foretold his own passing and was buried by a miracle beside a tzaddik. A guest wrote to the Rebbe, who advised the rosh yeshiva and his students to learn Chitas daily, and his legs began to heal.
display.lesson: Learning Chitas every day, Chumash, Tehillim and Tanya, brings great protection and blessing. Never delay helping someone in need, and never mock anyone.
